title: Security Advance with a Returned-Payment Replacement: Advance Months by Bank Returns
content:
**Rule.** On a Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement, a tenant with repeated bank returns adds a security advance to the replacement of a returned payment, held on the agreement as a credit balance toward the next rent. The advance months follow the payments reversed on the agreement for insufficient funds or a closed account in the 12 months up to the handling date:

| Such returns in the 12 months | Advance months |
|---|---|
| 4 or more | 2 |
| 2 or 3 | 1 |
| 1 | none |

The security advance is the advance months multiplied by the advance month — one month's rent as the agreement will bill it on its next due date — with the product rounded to the cent, half up, and the replacement amount is the balance due plus the security advance.

The returns are counted from the agreement's ledger: payment reversals whose reason is insufficient funds or account closed, posted in the 12 months up to the handling date. A card chargeback is not such a return.

## Edges

| Returns counted | Advance months |
|---|---|
| 1 | 0 |
| 2 | 1 |
| 3 | 1 |
| 4 | 2 |

## Hypothetical cases
- Bank returns in February, May and September of the 12 months: three returns, one advance month.
- A single bank return in the 12 months, plus a card chargeback: one return is counted, so no advance month is added and no security advance is taken.
